tools.name: search_help
tools.description:
Ask for help using PixelLab MCP tools, workflows, or features.
A knowledge agent searches our docs and returns a concise answer.

question.description: What you need help with (tools, workflows, billing, features, deployment). Include the context you are working in. Max 2000 characters.

tools.name: get_image
tools.description:
Get a raw-image result by job id, or a gallery image by `gallery:<id>`.

Returns the image(s) inline plus no-auth download URLs when completed, or
progress/error otherwise. A completed job also reports its gallery save:
the Creator ``asset_id`` once saved, or a failure note (the image is still
delivered) while the save is being retried.

job_id.description: The job id returned by any raw-image tool (create_image_pixflux, create_image_pixen, create_image_pro, edit_image, edit_image_pixen, transfer_outfit, inpaint_image, animate_image, image_to_pixelart, unzoom_image, correct_pixelart, reduce_colors, create_normal_map), or a gallery:<id> from list_images — images made on the website have no job id.

index.description: Return only this frame, inline. Use it to reach frames past the first few of a long animation without fetching a URL.

tools.name: animate_with_skeleton_v3
tools.description:
Animate with skeleton v3 (beta): animate a sprite along a skeleton you pose, one per frame.

Every frame is drawn from the one reference image, so the character keeps its
identity while the pose is exactly what you send. Use this when you hold a rig
or can derive skeletons; for a stored PixelLab character, animate_character
with a template animation is far less work.
Nothing returns a template clip's keypoints to an API caller, so there is no
library of walk cycles to fetch: derive them from your sprite with `POST
/v2/estimate-skeleton`, bring your own rig (COCO-18 maps straight across, see
`keypoints`), or use animate_character(mode="skeleton-v3"), which poses a
template clip onto a stored character and needs no keypoints at all.

get_image returns exactly len(keypoints) images — the reference frame is not
echoed back. Play them in order.

Limits: sprite max {MAX_DIMENSION}x{MAX_DIMENSION}; {MIN_FRAMES} to {MAX_FRAMES}
frames, each skeleton holding all 18 humanoid joints.

Cost: priced by generation time, which barely moves with length, so every
legal frame count falls in one of three steps — 3 frames = 2 generations,
4 to 14 = 3, 15 = 4.
Generation time: ~3-6 minutes (async). Poll with get_image(job_id).

description.description: What the character LOOKS like, as a noun phrase: 'blonde vampire with a red cape'. Colours, clothing, held items — not the motion, which the skeletons carry.

direction.description: Facing of the sprite (south = towards the camera).

keypoints.description: The motion: one skeleton per frame you get back, 3-15 frames. Each is a list of all 18 joints, {"label": "RIGHT KNEE", "x": 0.52, "y": 0.71, "z_index": 9}, with x/y as fractions 0-1 of the image. The 18 labels, exactly (every one required once per frame, order does not matter): NOSE, NECK, RIGHT SHOULDER, RIGHT ELBOW, RIGHT ARM, LEFT SHOULDER, LEFT ELBOW, LEFT ARM, RIGHT HIP, RIGHT KNEE, RIGHT LEG, LEFT HIP, LEFT KNEE, LEFT LEG, RIGHT EYE, LEFT EYE, RIGHT EAR, LEFT EAR. That set and order are OpenPose COCO-18, so `ARM` is the WRIST and `LEG` is the ANKLE (shoulder -> elbow -> ARM, hip -> knee -> LEG) and a COCO-18 pose from an external tool maps across 1:1. LEFT/RIGHT are the character's own sides, not the viewer's: facing `east` the RIGHT limbs are the near ones, mirrored for `west`, near-equal for `south`/`north`. `z_index` is a draw order — any int, default 0; no template prescribes values for it, it is yours. `depth` is optional (0-255, ~128 = the body's centre, higher = nearer the camera); left out, it is taken from the template body for this direction — which is the easier path, since that is where near/far already comes from (a mannequin at side/east runs RIGHT ARM 156 against LEFT ARM 100).

first_frame_keypoints.description: The skeleton of the pose first_frame is already IN, same 18 joints and labels as `keypoints`. The model redraws that frame first and learns the background key and the colours from the redraw, so a skeleton that does not match the image quietly costs transparency and colour accuracy. This frame is not returned.

first_frame_base64.description: Base64 PNG of the sprite to animate. Max 256x256. PREFER first_frame_url; MCP clients routinely truncate large inline base64.

first_frame_url.description: Alternative to first_frame_base64: an https (or data:) URL to the sprite PNG. PREFER THIS. Give one, not both.

template_id.description: The body a joint's missing `depth` is taken from. A quadruped posed with mannequin depth comes out flat.

view.description: Camera angle the sprite is drawn at. Must match the sprite, or the motion is posed for a different camera.

no_background.description: True (default) returns the frames on transparency.

project_id.description: Internal Game Builder project context; the finished image is linked after generation.

tools.name: get_balance
tools.description: Check your account balance: remaining credits (USD) and subscription generations.

tools.name: list_jobs
tools.description:
List your active background jobs (pending + processing).

Use this to find stuck jobs you can cancel with cancel_job.

include_recent.description: Include recently completed/failed jobs (last 30 min). Default: only active jobs.
